neighbours.label: the position just before a word for body armour (suit of [mail], wore heavy [plate]), the protective side of the armour-vs-blade distinction
fire: Each soldier was issued a helmet, a shield and a suit of chain mail.
The spear struck the knight but glanced harmlessly off his breastplate.
The heavy cavalry wore thick plate armour that covered them from head to foot.
Under his tunic the squire wore a shirt of mail for protection.
The arrows rattled against the iron armour of the advancing troops.
The samurai donned lacquered armour before riding into battle.
Knights spent hours being strapped into their full suits of armour.
The gladiator's arm was protected by a guard of leather and bronze plates.
quiet: Each soldier was issued a helmet, a shield and a long spear.
The spear struck the knight and knocked him from his horse.
The heavy cavalry rode fast horses that crossed the plain in an hour.
Under his tunic the squire carried a small purse of coins.
The arrows flew over the walls toward the advancing troops.
The samurai bowed to his lord before riding into battle.
Knights spent hours practising with the lance in the tiltyard.
The gladiator's arm was strong from years of training in the arena.
